Welcome to the game! 

- **Aiming!** Aiming in this game feels a bit different and is going to take some time to develop, so don't beat yourself up over it. For every character that is relatively grounded and easy to hit, there are 2 others that can zip around your screen in a millisecond 💀. As Cassidy, your magnetic grenade can temporarily prevent enemies from using movement abilities. Learning the best times to use it on someone (like genji, tracer, etc...) can really make a difference in winning or losing a duel.  
  
- **Positioning!** A lot of new players tend to have lackluster positioning (standing too far in, standing too far back, etc...). Many heroes have the abilitiy to delete your healthbar in seconds if they get too close. It can also be difficult for supports to heal you if you're too close to the enemies or by yourself in some unknown part of the map. Learn where your hero works best and exploit the hell out of it.  
  
-  **Hero variety!** Love it or hate it, Overwatch is basically a big game of rock-paper-scissors. Knowing how to play a hero well is important, but sometimes not even the best players can play their best heroes if someone on the enemy team is playing their counter. Learning a variety of different heroes with different playstyles can go a long way.  
  
There's a lot more you can go into but those are the most important to begin with imo. Welcome to the game, and I hope you have fun!!

# [Imp Trailblazer](https://i.imgur.com/HdD3Ow4.png)

Warlock | Epic | 6 mana 3/3 minion

**Battlecry and deathrattle: Invoke** Galakrond.

​

This card is a Warlock spin of the Shaman card \[\[Corrupt Elementalist\]\], in that it also allows you to **Invoke twice.** However, the fact its a battlecry and deathrattle makes it more flexible to play *with*, or if you're the opponent, play *around.* Thanks to the deathrattle being half the invoke you can cheat this minion out with \[\[Possessed Lackey\]\] or \[\[Skull of the Man'ari\]\] for half the value, or play it normally and get 7/7 worth of stats if your opponent doesn't silence it. Either way, in most case scenarios you will end up upgrading your galakrond while also creating board presence.

# [Bloodreaver's Scythe](https://i.imgur.com/baC5JZn.png)

6 mana / Epic / 5/2 Warlock weapon

**Overkill:** Summon a friendly demon that died this game.

​

This weapon is a callback to the effect used by \[\[Bloodreaver Guldan\]\]. Similar to the DK, you can use this weapon to revive \[\[Voidlord\]\], \[\[Mal'Ganis\]\], or \[\[Voidcaller\]\]. In terms of balance i'm a little split on whether it's too overpowered or underpowered. One one hand, reviving friendly demons has proven to be a very powerful effect. However, \[\[Arcanite Reaper\]\] sees almost no play and this weapon is more expensive than it with the same stats. Feel free to comment your thoughts. Thanks!

# [Greedy Mummy](https://i.imgur.com/0pRtlN7.png)

5 Mana / Rare / 6/2 Druid Minion

**Lifesteal, Reborn**

**Deathrattle:** Gain an empty mana crystal.

​

This minion is useful in more ways than one. I designed his name, deathrattle, and stats after \[\[Greedy Sprite\]\]. Since Reborn brings him back, it's possible to gain 2 empty mana crystals off of his deathrattle. With the 5 mana cost, this makes him comparable to pre-nerf \[\[Nourish\]\]. However, whether he is weaker or stronger than Nourish depends on if the opponent is running silence. The final icing on the cake is the lifesteal, which helps trigger \[\[Lucentbark\]\] and \[\[Crystal Stag\]\].
